Working/Functional Title

Senior Research Data Analyst

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the Assistant Vice President (AVP) of Operations, the Analyst serves as a key trusted advisor to ORI’s core leadership team. This role independently executes complex strategic data analysis, financial forecasting, and operational modeling that transcends traditional data compilation. Operating with an entrepreneurial mindset, the successful candidate will translate complex operational, federal, State, and institutional data into forward-looking strategic insights to actively drive fiscal sustainability, mitigate deficits, track ROI, and maximize high-impact, revenue-generating initiatives across the multi-million-dollar research enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Research Data Analysis & Advisory (40%)

Design and implement impact and ROI analysis for all strategic ORI initiatives, such as the National Security Initiative, internal funding programs (SPG, DFI, MSURF Post Doctoral Scholars Program), professorship programs and more.
Perform deep-dive analyses into institutional and departmental budgetary trends and changes, clearly communicating the narrative, macrolevel trends, and financial shifts.
Formulate clear, narrative-driven reports, executive summaries, and data visualizations to directly support executive decision-making.
Interpret findings to support recommendations based on the results of the analysis.

Predictive Forecasting & Scenario Modeling (35%)

Develop, maintain, and sophisticatedly model short- and long-term financial projections for the multi-million-dollar research enterprise.
Work with the Office of Sponsored Programs and other ORI units to build dynamic, "what-if" predictive models to simulate the fiscal impact of shifting federal funding landscapes, compliance changes, and new institutional initiatives.
Track, evaluate, and report on the fiscal health and ROI of ORI’s revenue-generating initiatives (e.g., corporate partnerships, technology transfer/commercialization revenue, and national security).

Collaboration within ORI and with Partner Units (10%)

Consult with ORI units, campus partners, and leadership to understand reporting needs.
Interpret analytical findings and recommend improvements to reporting tools and processes.

Training and Guidance (10%)

Develop training materials and provide guidance on reporting tools, dashboards, and data interpretation.

Special Projects and Committees (5%)

Conduct special projects and serve on cross-functional committees related to data initiatives and policy.

Core Competencies for Success

Business Acumen in Academia: Understands that a research enterprise operates both as an academic mission and as a complex business.
Forward-Thinking & Initiative-taking: Doesn't just report on past data but predicts future fiscal bottlenecks and opportunities.
Resilience & Agility: Thrives in a dynamic, high-momentum environment during periods of organizational growth and leadership transitions.

Minimum Requirements

Knowledge equivalent to that which normally would be acquired by completing one or two years of post-bachelor degree work, such as a Master's in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Analytics, Information Science, or another highly quantitative field. Three to five (3–5) years of related and progressively more responsible or expansive work experience in complex data analysis, financial modeling, strategic budgeting, or institutional forecasting; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Desired Qualifications

Higher Education/Research Experience: Prior financial or analytical experience within a major R1 research university, academic medical center, or complex organization dealing with federal grants, contract accounting, or Uniform Guidance compliance.
Business Intelligence Tools: Demonstrated experience designing, building, and supporting executive-level dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or comparable business intelligence platforms to support data-informed decision-making.
Strategic Problem Solving: Proven track record in deficit management, structural turnaround strategies, or designing self-sustaining revenue models for operational units.
Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with a proven ability to "tell the story behind the numbers" to non-financial stakeholders

Who We Are

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

The Cal-Bridge program is a partnership of all three segments of the California higher education system: 10 University of California (UC), 23 California State Universities (CSU), and 116 California Community College (CCC) campuses. The Cal-Bridge program consists of four distinct but interconnected programs: the undergraduate program, summer research program, doctoral program, and postdoctoral program, which together create a comprehensive, end-to-end pathway for undergraduate STEM majors from the diverse student population of the three systems through graduate school to a PhD, postdoctoral fellowship, and ultimately membership in the STEM professoriate or tech workforce.

The Cal-Bridge Undergraduate Program provides financial support, intensive mentoring and professional development for third- and fourth-year CSU students and sponsors summer research opportunities at major research institutions, with the goal of achieving competitiveness with their applications to PhD programs. The Cal-Bridge Summer research program provides research opportunities for CSU and CCC STEM undergraduates at UC campuses and leading research institutions nationwide. The Cal-Bridge Doctoral Program provides doctoral fellowships and focuses on professional development in the areas of research leadership and pedagogy, continued development of professional networks, and acculturation into leadership careers in academia, government, and industry. The doctoral program is open to Cal-Bridge undergraduate scholars who matriculate to a PhD program as well as UC LEADS undergraduates from Cal-Bridge majors who matriculate to a UC PhD program. The Cal-Bridge postdoctoral program, in partnership with the UC PPFP program, provides two-year postdoctoral fellowships at a UC or CSU campus, to further prepare scholars to become competitive faculty candidates.

Your Role on the Team

The University of California, Irvine is seeking a Doctoral Program Coordinator for Cal-Bridge. Under the direction of the Assistant Director for Administration and Finance, this position serves as the primary staff coordinator for doctoral and postdoctoral programs, working closely with program leadership to implement strategic initiatives, develop standard operating procedures, and drive continuous process improvements. Create systems to track outcomes and demographics including doctoral degrees and career outcomes. Attend and provide support for the doctoral Summer Institute. Coordinate contracts and logistics for Summer Research scholars at the UC’s. Coordinate contracts and logistics for FAST scholars at the CSUs. Financial Support

jobs.description:
We are seeking a Sr. Research Project Coordinator
who will oversee the day-to-day activities of a single complex or multiple research projects and makes independent decisions that impact the conduct of the research. Assists in goal setting and creating implementation plans. Contributes to budget formulation, communications, and data systems.

In collaboration with an engaged research team in Baltimore and Fort Peck Reservation, the Sr. Research Program Coordinator will work in partnership to coordinate the adaptation of the myPlan Teen intimate partner violence tech program for and with Indigenous youth in Montana. The position will utilize community-based research methodologies to facilitate community consultations and youth engagement in the Fort Peck Community.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Assist Principal Investigator or more senior research staff to ensure operational feasibility of proposed protocol/study design.
Develop standard operating procedures and data collection forms based on understanding of underlying study design.
Develop or oversee design and implementation of study procedures and tools for data collection, e.g. participant interviews, administer questionnaires; background research, laboratory processing, etc.
Ensure compliance with all protocols, procedures, and applicable regulations.
Participate in developing study budget.
Set up data collection system and ensure validity of study data.
Organize and quality control study data
Recommend and implement changes to protocol operations based on results and goals.
Conduct literature searches to provide background information.
Abstract and index information based on knowledge of subject matter.
Other duties as assigned.

In addition to the duties described above

Work with the Principal Investigators and study team to coordinate app content adaptations, ensuring content of myPlan app is culturally relevant, accurate, research-backed, and trauma-informed.
Present to partners and facilitate community consultations and Tribal Advisory Board meetings related to the app.
Manage relationships with community partnerships, schools, and advisory board members.
Based at Fort Peck, located in Montana, to support on-site study team members in project implementation, recruitment, data collection, and data dissemination.

Bachelor’s Degree in a related field.
Three years of related experience.
Additional education may substitute for required experience and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Master's Degree in a related field.
Collaborative and relationship building skills, able to build trust with community members and leaders.
Experience working in rural and remote reservation settings. Based in Fort Peck, Montana.

The Cal-Bridge program is a partnership of all three segments of the California higher education system: 10 University of California (UC), 23 California State Universities (CSU), and 116 California Community College (CCC) campuses. The Cal-Bridge program consists of four distinct but interconnected programs: the undergraduate program, summer research program, doctoral program, and postdoctoral program, which together create a comprehensive, end-to-end pathway for undergraduate STEM majors from the diverse student population of the three systems through graduate school to a PhD, postdoctoral fellowship, and ultimately membership in the STEM professoriate or tech workforce.

The Cal-Bridge Undergraduate Program provides financial support, intensive mentoring and professional development for third- and fourth-year CSU students and sponsors summer research opportunities at major research institutions, with the goal of achieving competitiveness with their applications to PhD programs. The Cal-Bridge Summer research program provides research opportunities for CSU and CCC STEM undergraduates at UC campuses and leading research institutions nationwide. The Cal-Bridge Doctoral Program provides doctoral fellowships and focuses on professional development in the areas of research leadership and pedagogy, continued development of professional networks, and acculturation into leadership careers in academia, government, and industry. The doctoral program is open to Cal-Bridge undergraduate scholars who matriculate to a PhD program as well as UC LEADS undergraduates from Cal-Bridge majors who matriculate to a UC PhD program. At EA, you’ll find yourself surrounded by dynamic professionals that embrace collaboration and curiosity to foster innovation and problem-solving.
